questions.question: What is system design?

options.text: Defining architecture of a software system

questions.explanation: System design defines how components interact to build scalable software.

questions.question: What does scalability mean?

options.text: Ability to handle growth in users or load

questions.explanation: Scalability means handling increased traffic or data.

questions.question: What is horizontal scaling?

options.text: Adding more CPU to a server

questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds more machines.

questions.question: What is vertical scaling?
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling upgrades CPU/RAM of a single machine.

questions.question: What is load balancing?
questions.explanation: Load balancers distribute traffic to prevent overload.

questions.question: What is a database index?

options.text: A structure to speed up queries

questions.explanation: Indexes improve read performance.

questions.question: What is caching?

options.text: Storing data temporarily for fast access

questions.explanation: Caching reduces latency and DB load.

questions.question: Which cache is commonly used in backend systems?
questions.explanation: Redis is widely used for in-memory caching.

questions.question: What is a CDN?
questions.explanation: CDNs serve content from nearest locations.

questions.question: What problem does CDN solve?
questions.explanation: CDN reduces latency by serving content closer to users.

questions.question: What is a monolithic architecture?
questions.explanation: Monoliths bundle all logic in one app.

questions.question: What is microservices architecture?
questions.explanation: Microservices split systems into independent services.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used between microservices?
questions.explanation: REST over HTTP is commonly used.

questions.question: What is a single point of failure?

options.text: Component whose failure crashes entire system

questions.explanation: Single point failures reduce reliability.

questions.question: What is high availability?
questions.explanation: High availability ensures minimal downtime.

questions.question: What is database replication?
questions.explanation: Replication improves availability and reads.

questions.question: What is sharding?
questions.explanation: Sharding distributes data across nodes.

questions.question: Which system is best for asynchronous tasks?
questions.explanation: Queues handle background processing.

questions.question: Example of message queue?
questions.explanation: RabbitMQ is a popular message broker.

questions.question: What is eventual consistency?
questions.explanation: Used in distributed systems.

questions.question: CAP theorem stands for?
questions.explanation: CAP theorem defines distributed system trade-offs.

questions.question: What is API?
questions.explanation: APIs enable communication between systems.

questions.question: Why is authentication important?
questions.explanation: Authentication verifies user identity.

questions.question: What is authorization?
questions.explanation: Authorization defines access rights.

questions.question: First step in system design interview?
questions.explanation: Clarifying requirements is critical.
